title: Moses fears speaking — Exodus 4
paragraphs: He just didn’t believe he had the mouth for it.

In Exodus 4, Moses is not lazy. He is afraid. God calls him to confront Pharaoh, and Moses answers with the ache many of us hide: “I am not eloquent… I am slow of speech and of tongue” (Exodus 4:10). He is basically saying, “Lord, You picked the wrong man.”
And that is where the fire starts.

Because God does not comfort Moses by praising his talent. He answers with power: “Who has made man’s mouth?... Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall speak” (Exodus 4:11–12). The issue was never Moses’ weakness. The issue was whether Moses would trust the God who made him.

Moses’ fear of speaking was deeper than stage fright. It was the terror of inadequacy. The shame of not feeling enough. The panic that obedience would expose his weakness in public. And that is still our struggle. We say, “I can’t lead. I can’t preach. I can’t share the Gospel. I’m not ready.” Yet God has always loved using trembling people so His glory, not their polish, gets seen.
Still, Moses hesitates again: “Oh, my Lord, please send someone else” (Exodus 4:13). That is not just insecurity anymore. That is resistance. Fear, if left unchecked, can become disobedience.
And that’s where grace walks in.

God does not throw Moses away. He provides Aaron. He still sends him. He still uses him. Mercy meets the man who is shaking. What a Savior. Even in our weakness, God is patient. Even when our faith limps, He does not cancel His calling so quickly.

Because Jesus is the better and greater Deliverer. Where Moses trembled, Christ obeyed perfectly. Where Moses feared the mission, Jesus set His face toward the cross. And through His death and resurrection, He saves sinners, restores the ashamed, and fills weak people with boldness by His Spirit. Your stutter does not scare Him. Your insecurity does not disqualify you. Your past does not silence His grace.

God is not waiting for you to become impressive.
He is calling you to become obedient.

Open your mouth.
Tell the truth.
Share Christ.
And trust the God who made your mouth.

“I will be with your mouth.”
That word still carries power.
